cursor-team-kit/skills/make-pr-easy-to-r.note: adopt-rule: destination finishing-a-development-branch, which held only "Force-push without explicit request" and no content-preservation guard. Adopted as the principle, not the source's recipe: its check captures origin/<head>^{tree}, so any unpushed commit makes it false-alarm. Two further drafts were disproved in scratch repos before this landed. Tree-hash equality survives squash, reorder, reword and --force-rebase, but only while the base is unchanged. Across a moved base neither literal `git diff` equality nor `git patch-id` is sound: the former breaks whenever upstream touches the same file at all, the latter once upstream changes a line inside the few lines of context around the hunk (a distant edit leaves patch-id intact, measured at 3 lines of context), and both then report a clean carry as a failure. What shipped is `git range-diff` with an explicit --creation-factor=99, because at the default a cleanly carried commit whose context moved can print `<` as though it had vanished, and every marker other than `=` is stated as a prompt to inspect rather than a verdict — a correctly resolved conflict is marked the same as a botched one.

thermos/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quali.note: duplicate — byte-identical to cursor-team-kit/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review/SKILL.md (confirmed: both 193 lines, same frontmatter, same content at every sampled offset), and therefore duplicate of reviewing-for-bloat for the same reasons.

thermos/skills/thermo-nuclear-review.note: adopt-rule → requesting-code-review. Bug/security/regression review is owned by prompts/code-reviewer.md ('Security concerns?', severity categorization, 'Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.'). The mechanism the corpus lacks is an anchoring guard: a reviewer must complete its own audit BEFORE reading BugBot/other reviewers' comments on the PR, then fold in and attribute what they found. Corpus reviewer prompt has no ordering rule against prior findings.

thermos/skills/thermos.note: reject — product-coupled workflow-recipe. Five steps that launch two hardcoded Cursor subagent slugs (`thermo-nuclear-review-subagent`, `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review-subagent`) with `run_in_background: true`, then summarize. The one portable idea (weight findings that two independent reviewers both raise) is a sentence, and dispatching-parallel-agents already owns the fan-out/integrate procedure.

third_party/x/skills/x-api-mcp-guide.evidence: read in full (3116w). Frontmatter carries the policy; body is X API surface.
third_party/x/skills/x-api-mcp-guide.note: Portable shape is real: check the balance before the operation, estimate cost before an expensive call, and distinguish an empty account from a broken setup (tools=0 is a setup failure, not a paywall). No corpus skill owns paid-API cost policy, and one rule harvested from a vendor guide does not justify a new skill.

method: All 91 SKILL.md files enumerated from the tree at the pinned sha; every file carries exactly one disposition, asserted to sum to 91. 74 were assessed by three scout audits. The remaining 17 were initially dispositioned from descriptions alone, then read in full (plus 11 companion files), which overturned that verdict on 8 and produced 3 further adoptions. Two Benny rows outside those 17 were verified by targeted grep rather than a full read; their evidence fields say so. Two adopt-skill candidates were refused on RED-baseline evidence rather than on judgement: control agents satisfied the proposed rules unaided.
caveat: Verdicts come from three scout audits of differing strictness. AuditPstackWorkflows applied a visibly laxer bar than AuditTeamKitThermos: it returned adopt-rule for workflow recipes with hardcoded model slugs (arena, architect, why, teach, figure-it-out) of the same class AuditTeamKitThermos rejected (review-and-ship, new-branch-and-pr). An independent oracle pass read 14 of the 19 unlanded adopt-rule rows and found roughly 20% survive as stated, 30-40% yield any edit at all, none yields a section. Treat adopt-* as a lead list, not a work queue.

statusMeaning.landed: Adopted into the corpus; landedIn names the destination.
statusMeaning.pending: adopt-* verdict from a scout audit, NOT yet assessed by the oracle pass or actioned. See `caveat` — roughly 20% survive scrutiny as stated. A lead, not a task.
statusMeaning.no-action: duplicate, reject, or product-specific. No corpus change warranted.

schema.landedIn: commit sha plus destination; present iff status is landed
